Get started with kplotly.r

Source: vignettes/kplotly.Rmd
kplotly.Rmd

kplotly() draws an interactive plotly.js graphic from a single call and returns a kplotly object that you can compose, modify, or turn into an htmlwidget. Its arguments are those of kggplot::kggplot(): switching a call from a static to an interactive plot is a matter of changing the function name.

plotly.js is embedded in the package (the “cartesian” bundle), so kplotly.r only depends on htmlwidgets, not on the plotly R package.

Time series

A Date or POSIXct x gives a line, a range slider under the x axis and a hover that shows every series at the hovered date. Several y columns (or "all") are stacked and coloured by series.

set.seed(1)
weather <- data.frame(date = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:364)
weather$rain <- rgamma(365, 0.4, 0.1)
weather$temp <- 12 + 8 * sin(1:365 / 58 - 1.5) + rnorm(365)
kplotly(weather, "date", c("rain", "temp"), title = "Weather in 2024")

The vars argument of kplot and TSstudio style calls is accepted, and slider turns the range slider on or off:

kplotly(weather, vars = list(x = "date", y = "all"), type = "point",
        slider = FALSE)

A ts object works too:

kplotly(AirPassengers, title = "Air passengers", theme = "minimal")

Types, colours and sizes

The type is guessed from x (line for dates, point for numbers, bar for categories) or set with type: kply_types() lists them.

kply_types()
#> [1] "point" "line"  "step"  "area"  "bar"   "col"
kplotly(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species",
        size = "Petal.Width", theme = "bw")

A string that is not a column names the layer in the legend, and I() gives a fixed value:

obs <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2 + rnorm(20))
sim <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2)
kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point") +
  kplotly(sim, "t", "v", color = I("black"), type = "line")

Composing plots

+ superposes plots: colours are shared and a legend entry is shown once; clicking it hides the level in every layer.

kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point") +
  kplotly(sim, "t", "v", color = "Simulated", type = "line") +
  kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "line",
          line = list(dash = "dot"))

Pipe-friendly modifiers change a plot afterwards:

kplotly(weather, "date", "temp") |>
  kply_add(type = "point", opacity = 0.4) |>
  kply_labs(title = "Temperature", y = "°C") |>
  kply_theme("inrae") |>
  kply_legend("bottom")

Themes and palettes 

kply_themes()
#> [1] "default" "minimal" "bw"      "inrae"
kply_palettes()
#> [1] "plotly"    "inrae"     "okabe_ito"
kplotly(weather, "date", c("rain", "temp"), theme = "inrae")

palette takes a palette name, colours (named to fix the colour of a level) or a function of n.

Going further with plotly.js

Any plotly.js attribute is reachable:

  • trace attributes in the ... of kplotly() (line = list(width = 1), opacity, connectgaps…);
  • layout attributes with kply_layout(), configuration with kply_config();
  • a function of the htmlwidget added with +, applied last (e.g. htmlwidgets::onRender()).
kplotly(weather, "date", "rain", type = "bar") |>
  kply_layout(yaxis = list(type = "log")) |>
  kply_config(locale = "fr")

as_htmlwidget() returns the widget, for Shiny (htmlwidgets::shinyRenderWidget()) or to save it; kply_save() writes an HTML file.

Extending kplotly.r

Types, themes and palettes live in registries:

kply_register_type(
  "linepoint", list(type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers"),
  color = c("marker.color", "line.color"), sort = TRUE
)
kply_register_palette("traffic", c("#2ecc71", "#f1c40f", "#e74c3c"))
kply_register_theme("traffic", list(plot_bgcolor = "#fafafa"),
                    palette = "traffic")
kplotly(pressure, "temperature", "pressure", type = "linepoint",
        theme = "traffic")

A new input class needs an as_kdata() method returning a data frame.
